question: What is the primary cause of neonatal tetanus?

options.A: Severe dehydration during the first week of life
options.B: Congenital weakness of the newborn immune system
options.C: A viral infection passed through breast milk
options.D: A neurotoxin produced by Clostridium tetani

explanation: You got this! Neonatal tetanus happens when a powerful toxin released by the bacterium Clostridium tetani attacks a baby's nervous system.

question: Which symptom is a major warning sign of botulism poisoning from Clostridium botulinum?

options.A: Severe joint swelling and stiffness
options.B: High fever and immediate skin rashes
options.C: Rapid hair loss within twenty-four hours
options.D: Muscle paralysis affecting the nervous system

explanation: Clostridium botulinum makes a potent neurotoxin that blocks nerve signals, leading to muscle weakness and paralysis. Safety first with canned and preserved foods!

question: What is the main thing you must check before letting a patient drink water after a throat-numbing laryngoscopy?

options.A: The passage of urine into the bedside commode
options.B: A stable body temperature for two hours
options.C: The return of the gag reflex and swallowing ability
options.D: A completely normal blood pressure reading

explanation: You got it! Always wait for the numbing medicine to wear off and the gag reflex to come back so they don't choke or aspirate water.

question: Which of these is NOT part of a holistic palliative assessment?

options.A: Respecting cultural beliefs and family traditions
options.B: Strictly monitoring laboratory blood cell counts
options.C: Evaluating emotional and psychological well-being
options.D: Listening to spiritual and existential concerns

explanation: While lab results matter in acute care, palliative care is all about the human experience—feelings, culture, and spirit. It's much more than just numbers on a lab sheet!

question: Why should you never use both hands to recap a used needle?

options.A: It bends the needle tip and makes the injection painful
options.B: It drastically increases the risk of an accidental needle-stick injury
options.C: It violates hospital policies regarding medication waste disposal
options.D: It takes too much time during a busy medication round

explanation: Using two hands to recap makes it way too easy to miss the cap and puncture your own finger. Safety first—keep that hand away from the sharp end!

question: What major public health threat is directly worsened by the over-prescription of antibiotics?

options.A: High blood pressure rates
options.B: Chronic kidney stone disease
options.C: Antimicrobial resistance
options.D: Nutritional vitamin deficiencies

explanation: Unnecessary antibiotic use teaches bacteria how to survive drug treatments, creating resistant strains that are hard to cure. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is the main goal of performing the Romberg test during a physical exam?

options.A: To check the integrity of cranial nerve eight
options.B: To evaluate the patient's balance and proprioception
options.C: To determine the patient's short-term memory
options.D: To measure the strength of the quadriceps muscle

explanation: The Romberg test checks how well the body keeps its balance with eyes closed. Always stand close by to catch them if they sway!

question: Why should nurses recommend locally available, affordable foods during nutritional counseling?

options.A: Local foods completely replace the need for drugs
options.B: Expensive imported foods have zero nutrients
options.C: Patients refuse to eat anything foreign
options.D: It ensures the dietary advice is realistic and sustainable

explanation: Spot on! Good nursing advice must fit the patient's real life and pocket so they can actually follow it.

question: A 15-year-old girl comes to the clinic with her older husband, showing bruises and sadness. How should the nurse care for her?

options.A: Scold the husband in front of the patient and demand they divorce immediately
options.B: Report the family to the hospital billing department for financial investigation
options.C: Use a trauma-informed approach, ensure privacy for screening, and connect her with social support
options.D: Treat the physical bruises quickly and send them home without asking further questions

explanation: You've got it! Keeping her safe, checking her emotional needs, and involving social services is the hallmark of great, compassionate nursing.

question: Why must we encourage patients to drink plenty of water right after a barium meal?

options.A: To prevent the patient from developing a high fever
options.B: To prevent severe constipation caused by the barium
options.C: To dissolve any leftover barium remaining in the stomach
options.D: To speed up the absorption of the contrast into the blood

explanation: Spot on! Barium soaks up water like a sponge as it moves down, so extra fluids save your patient from a hard, painful time in the toilet. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h6)

question: Why does the stomach have an extra layer of muscle compared to other parts of the digestive tract?

options.A: To allow vigorous multi-directional churning of solid food
options.B: To absorb nutrients directly into the bloodstream very quickly
options.C: To store extra blood supply for active digestive processes
options.D: To prevent digestive enzymes from burning through the wall

explanation: Food isn't always liquid! That extra muscle layer gives the stomach extra power to twist and mash solid food into a smooth mixture.

question: What should a QA committee do if there is a sudden increase in surgical wound infections?

options.A: Close the entire hospital permanently
options.B: Blame the patients for having weak immune systems
options.C: Ignore the data because infections are normal after surgery
options.D: Investigate sterilization practices and surgical routines right away

explanation: You got it! A sudden jump in infections is a red flag that requires an immediate check of theatre and ward cleanliness.

question: After a severe heart attack, why is the long-term recovery of heart muscle function often limited?

options.A: Cardiac cells divide much faster than epithelial cells, causing chaotic overgrowth
options.B: The cutaneous membrane prevents blood from reaching the damaged chest muscle
options.C: Cardiac muscle tissue has very limited ability to regenerate and is often replaced by scar tissue
options.D: Smooth muscle completely takes over and alters the heart rate permanently

explanation: Heart muscle cells don't easily multiply to fix themselves. Instead, the body patches the area with scar tissue, which doesn't contract.

question: During an upper limb check, which finding means you need to report to the doctor right away?

options.A: Warm and pink nail beds
options.B: Normal breathing rate and rhythm
options.C: Strong grip strength in both hands
options.D: New numbness or tingling in the fingers

explanation: Numbness and tingling are red flags! They tell you a nerve might be pinched or irritated and needs urgent attention.

question: How should you document an adverse event in the patient's clinical chart?

options.A: Include notes about the hospital management being careless
options.B: Record objective clinical findings and nursing interventions clearly
options.C: Write down personal opinions about which coworker made the mistake
options.D: Avoid mentioning the event entirely to prevent patient anxiety

explanation: Keep your charting strictly factual! Write down only what you see, assess, and do for the patient.

question: What is the main job of the CSSD in a hospital?

options.A: Dispensing prescription medications to wards
options.B: Processing and sterilizing reusable medical equipment
options.C: Disposing of hazardous chemical waste
options.D: Managing patient admission records

explanation: The Central Sterilizing Supply Department (CSSD) is like the hospital's powerhouse for cleanliness! They clean, package, sterilize, and distribute all the medical tools used across the wards.

question: What is the very first step in the disease surveillance cycle?

options.A: Data generation and collection
options.B: Writing a newspaper advertisement
options.C: Publishing a textbook on epidemiology
options.D: Allocating national budget funds

explanation: It all starts right at the frontline! Nurses and health workers spot and record cases, kicking off the whole surveillance process.

question: Why do nurses wear sterile gloves when cleaning a fresh wound?

options.A: It blocks the portal of entry for pathogens into the wound
options.B: It destroys all bacteria living in the hospital air
options.C: It cures any underlying chronic illness
options.D: It transforms a susceptible host into an immune host

explanation: Spot on! Gloves act as a protective shield, stopping germs from sneaking into the open wound and breaking the infection chain.

question: Within what window of time should standard levonorgestrel emergency pills be taken for the best result?

options.A: Within 14 days of unprotected intercourse
options.B: At any time during the entire monthly cycle
options.C: Exactly 24 hours after the next menstrual period
options.D: Within 72 hours of unprotected intercourse

explanation: Levonorgestrel (like the popular Postinor-2) works best when taken within 72 hours (3 days) after unprotected sex. Keep this rule of thumb handy!

question: What happens to digestion when a woman goes into active labour?

options.A: It slows down significantly or stops almost entirely
options.B: It reverses direction, causing constant vomiting
options.C: It remains completely unchanged from normal pre-pregnancy rates
options.D: It speeds up to clear the body for delivery

explanation: The stress and pain of labour naturally put digestion on pause, meaning food stays in the stomach instead of moving along.

question: What does a 'null hypothesis' usually say about two groups being compared?

options.A: The first group always has a higher score
options.B: The second group received a better treatment
options.C: There is no real difference between them
options.D: There are not enough patients in the study

explanation: The null hypothesis assumes a boring baseline: that your new treatment didn't actually do anything special and the groups are essentially the same.

question: A nurse accidentally pricks a finger with a used needle of unknown status. What is the very first thing to do?

options.A: Fill out an incident report form for the hospital human resources
options.B: Begin taking a 28-day course of antibiotics immediately
options.C: Call the patient back to the clinic for a rapid blood test
options.D: Wash the puncture wound thoroughly with soap and clean water

explanation: Correct! Immediate first aid means rushing to wash the site with soap and water to rinse away germs.

question: What would an occupational therapist most likely help a recovering stroke patient do?

options.A: Rebuilding leg strength to walk up a flight of stairs
options.B: Practicing how to safely button a shirt and brush teeth
options.C: Navigating financial assistance for home medical equipment
options.D: Adjusting medication dosages for blood pressure control

explanation: You nailed it! Occupational therapists (OTs) focus on everyday tasks like dressing and grooming, while physical therapists focus on big movements like walking.

question: Why is treating an infected person usually not enough to stop a parasite outbreak on its own?

options.A: Patients are easily reinfected from their unimproved home environment
options.B: Parasites mutate into viral pathogens inside the human host
options.C: Laboratory tests cannot confirm when a patient is cured
options.D: Medications lose their potency immediately after leaving the clinic

explanation: If we cure a patient but send them back to dirty water and poor sanitation, they'll just catch the same worms all over again. We have to fix the environment too!

question: A patient with a degenerative condition frequently becomes exhausted halfway through a morning walk. What physical therapy strategy should be introduced?

options.A: Energy conservation and activity pacing
options.B: Complete bed rest to eliminate all physical exertion
options.C: Immediate removal of all walking aids
options.D: High-intensity weight lifting to build sudden bulk

explanation: Teaching the patient to pace themselves and conserve energy helps them stay active without burning out all their strength at once. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h4)

question: You discover that a contaminated oxygen machine is spreading a bacterial infection in your ward. What is your very first action?

options.A: Wait until all patients finish their breathing treatments before cleaning
options.B: Rinse the exterior surface quickly with ordinary tap water
options.C: Leave the machine in place but place a warning sign on the wall
options.D: Remove the equipment from service for proper cleaning and sterilization

explanation: Safety first! Take the dirty equipment out of action immediately so no more patients are exposed while you arrange for proper sterilization.

question: Why do our bones and muscles naturally change as we grow older?

options.A: Complete cessation of red blood cell production
options.B: Normal cumulative wear and tear over time
options.C: Rapid overgrowth of cartilage in major joints
options.D: A sudden failure of the endocrine system

explanation: Think of it like a well-used machine! Years of movement mean gradual, lifelong changes in our bone density, joint padding, and muscle fibers.

question: Which vein is located in the antecubital fossa and is often used for emergency access or blood draws?

options.A: Digital dorsal vein
options.B: Median cubital vein
options.C: Temporal scalp vein
options.D: Great saphenous vein

explanation: The median cubital vein sits right in the bend of the elbow, making it large, prominent, and easy to access quickly. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T16#GNS122_U1_T16_h2)

question: What is a well-known long-term issue for people who survive Lassa fever?

options.A: Loss of vision
options.B: Chronic kidney failure
options.C: Deafness
options.D: Permanent limb paralysis

explanation: Hearing loss is quite common after recovering from Lassa fever, and unfortunately, it can sometimes be permanent.

question: A cardiac monitor shows a high heart rate for a patient who is lying quietly in bed. What should you do next?

options.A: Unplug all the chest electrodes to stop the reading
options.B: Quickly give a strong heart medication
options.C: Assume the monitor is broken and turn off the alarm
options.D: Check the patient for pain, fever, or anxiety before reacting

explanation: Tachycardia can happen because of pain, stress, or fever—not just a machine error. Always investigate the clinical cause first. You're doing great!

question: How is explanatory research different from just watching patients in the ward?

options.A: Explanatory research requires no data collection from actual human subjects
options.B: Explanatory research looks for the underlying reasons behind an event, not just the facts
options.C: Observation is done by doctors while explanatory research is strictly for nursing students
options.D: Observation uses numerical data while explanatory research only uses spoken stories

explanation: Great thinking! While regular observation just shows us what is happening, explanatory research digs deeper to find the exact causes.

question: What is the most crucial safety step before placing a hot water bottle on your patient?

options.A: Checking the patient's current blood glucose level
options.B: Testing the temperature of the water and checking the skin
options.C: Asking the patient to sign a formal surgical consent form
options.D: Giving the patient a heavy sleeping pill

explanation: Safety first! Always test the water temperature yourself and check the skin condition to prevent accidental burns.

question: Why is the recovery phase just as important as the active response phase?

options.A: It is the only time nurses are legally allowed to administer medications.
options.B: It helps the community rebuild infrastructure and restore long-term health.
options.C: It prevents disasters from ever happening again in the future.
options.D: It replaces the need for any pre-disaster planning or drills.

explanation: Exactly! Recovery is all about long-term healing, fixing damaged buildings, and supporting the mental health of survivors over months or years.

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical feature of serum sickness?

options.A: Swollen lymph nodes in the neck
options.B: Permanent paralysis of the legs
options.C: Joint pain in the hands and knees
options.D: Persistent high fever

explanation: Serum sickness can make you feel miserable with rashes, fever, and aching joints, but it doesn't cause permanent paralysis.

question: What actually happens to a heart valve when a patient has stenosis?

options.A: It becomes stiff and fails to open fully.
options.B: It dissolves completely into the bloodstream.
options.C: It turns into muscle tissue.
options.D: It fails to close and leaks backward.

explanation: Stenosis simply means narrowing or stiffness. The valve flaps get stiff and won't swing wide open, making it hard for blood to flow forward.

question: What is the most important first step when doing a physical assessment on an FGM survivor?

options.A: Calling law enforcement immediately
options.B: Administering a strong general anesthetic
options.C: Establishing trust and ensuring informed consent
options.D: Photocopying her identification documents

explanation: You got it! Survivors may feel vulnerable or traumatized, so building a safe, trusting connection and getting clear consent before any exam is vital. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T8#GNS312_U1_T8_h3)

question: What is usually the very first step public health teams take when investigating a suspected disease outbreak?

options.A: Hold a press conference on national television
options.B: Close down all schools and markets in the entire country
options.C: Burn medical waste to destroy any remaining bacteria
options.D: Verify the diagnosis and confirm that an outbreak actually exists

explanation: Correct! Before launching a full investigation, health workers must make sure laboratory results and case numbers truly point to an outbreak.

question: Why does a baby facing forward (occiput posterior position) often cause a long labour?

options.A: It softens the cervix too early before contractions even begin.
options.B: It forces a wider diameter of the fetal head to fit through the pelvic dimensions.
options.C: It immediately causes the placenta to detach from the uterine wall.
options.D: It completely stops the mother from breathing deeply during contractions.

explanation: Well done. When the baby's head faces the mum's tummy instead of her back, it cannot squeeze through the pelvis as easily, causing a traffic jam!

question: How does culture influence a person's health-seeking habits?

options.A: It dictates the exact laboratory values for blood pressure
options.B: It determines the anatomical structure of human organs
options.C: It prevents individuals from ever feeling physical pain
options.D: It shapes how they view, express, and seek treatment for sickness

explanation: Culture guides our beliefs! It teaches us how to talk about pain, who to consult first, and what healing should look like.

question: Which factor is most important when deciding if a medicine belongs on an essential drug list?

options.A: How recently the drug was invented in a laboratory
options.B: National disease prevalence and public health needs
options.C: The marketing budget of the manufacturing company
options.D: Whether the drug is packaged in a colorful container

explanation: Exactly! We pick drugs based on the actual illnesses that trouble our local communities the most.

question: What is the job of the obturator when putting in a tracheostomy tube?

options.A: To connect the tube directly to the oxygen tubing
options.B: To catch dried mucus inside the main shaft
options.C: To inflate the internal balloon and seal the airway
options.D: To guide the outer cannula smoothly through the stoma

explanation: The obturator has a smooth, rounded tip. It slips inside the tube to make sure the edges don't scratch or damage the tissue when you guide it in. Smooth and safe!

question: Why must you feel (palpate) both rods of a Jadelle implant before trying to remove them?

options.A: To check if the hormone has completely changed color inside the body
options.B: To confirm the exact location of each rod and avoid missing a retained piece
options.C: To measure how much weight the client has gained since the insertion date
options.D: To make sure the local anesthetic has completely frozen the entire arm

explanation: Since Jadelle has two rods, you always want to locate both beforehand so you don't accidentally leave one behind in the arm!

question: Which international agreement is specifically dedicated to stopping discrimination against women?

options.A: UNICEF
options.B: CEDAW
options.C: AFCTA
options.D: WHO

explanation: CEDAW stands for the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women—a key global pact for women's rights!

question: An older stroke patient says their biggest goal is to walk to the backyard garden to see flowers. How should you use this?

options.A: Ignore the statement because garden visits are not medical milestones
options.B: Tell the patient to pick a standard treadmill speed instead
options.C: Incorporate the garden walk into realistic, patient-centered goal setting
options.D: Discharge the patient immediately since they have outdoor desires

explanation: You've got this! When rehab goals matter personally to the patient, they feel much more motivated to work hard and get better.

question: A community health nurse notices resistance to a new vaccination drive due to rumors in a village. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Ignore the rumors and continue giving vaccines only to those who walk in
options.B: Engage local community leaders to educate residents and address concerns
options.C: Call the police to force villagers to report for immediate immunization
options.D: Cancel the vaccination program and withdraw staff from the village

explanation: Spot on! Working hand-in-hand with trusted village leaders is the best way to clear up doubts, build trust, and help the community stay healthy.

question: The sagittal suture connects which two bones of the foetal skull?

options.A: The frontal and parietal bones
options.B: The two parietal bones
options.C: The temporal and frontal bones
options.D: The parietal and occipital bones

explanation: Think of the sagittal suture as the line running right down the middle of the top of the head, joining the left and right parietal bones together!

question: How many rods make up the Implanon NXT contraceptive implant system?

options.A: One rod
options.B: Two rods
options.C: Four rods
options.D: Six rods

explanation: Implanon NXT is a single-rod etonogestrel implant that provides up to three years of contraceptive protection. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T014#GNS226_U6_T014_h3)

question: Which scrotal condition feels like a 'bag of worms' when a nurse feels the area during an exam?

options.A: Varicocele
options.B: Epididymitis
options.C: Hydrocele
options.D: Orchitis

explanation: A varicocele happens when veins in the scrotum become swollen and twisted, giving them that classic, bumpy 'bag of worms' feel.

question: You notice a red patch over a patient's lower back that does not turn white when you press it with your finger. What does this usually mean?

options.A: A normal reaction to sleeping on cotton sheets
options.B: An early stage pressure injury starting to form
options.C: A healing bruise from a previous minor fall
options.D: An allergic reaction to bath soap

explanation: Great catch! When skin stays red and doesn't blanch (turn white) under pressure, it's a key early warning sign that deep tissue is suffering from a lack of blood flow.

question: You walk into a patient's room and see a big loop of chest tube tubing resting on the floor. What should you do first?

options.A: Clamp the chest tube immediately and page the physician for urgent removal
options.B: Lift the drainage canister up and place it on the patient's bed
options.C: Adjust the tubing so it coils loosely on the bed and drains freely without kinks
options.D: Disconnect the tubing joints to empty the pooled fluid onto the floor

explanation: Spot on! Dependent loops trap fluid and block drainage. Arranging the tubing neatly on the bed lets everything flow smoothly again.

question: Why is a good referral system so important for a client's reproductive rights?

options.A: It gives nurses full authority to choose which contraceptive a client must use
options.B: It forces clients to accept permanent contraceptive methods
options.C: It prevents clients from visiting traditional birth attendants
options.D: It ensures clients can access their preferred method even if local stock runs out

explanation: Clients have the right to choose what works for their bodies. If your clinic runs out of a specific supply, referring them elsewhere protects that choice!

question: Why is strict waste segregation vital during home visits?

options.A: It prevents the spread of infection to the family and community
options.B: It eliminates the need for hand washing after care
options.C: It makes the nurse finish the visit much faster
options.D: It reduces the total weight of the home visiting kit bag

explanation: Separating infectious and hazardous waste stops germs from spreading into the local environment and harming others. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h5)

question: Why must a nurse never turn their back on an open sterile field?

options.A: The sterile items will immediately slide off the tray
options.B: It looks unprofessional to the patient
options.C: You cannot see if something unsterile contaminates it
options.D: Air currents will blow the sterile drape away

explanation: Visual contact is required to guarantee that no unsterile object or person has breached the sterile zone. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of providing regular supportive supervision visits to rural community midwives?

options.A: To increase the paperwork burden without providing clinical assistance
options.B: To offer mentorship, solve operational challenges, and reduce professional isolation
options.C: To look for minor errors so the midwife can be publicly punished
options.D: To replace the midwife with an administrative clerk from the city

explanation: Supportive supervision focuses on guidance, problem-solving, and emotional encouragement rather than fault-finding, keeping rural health workers motivated. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h8)

question: Which nursing action is most helpful for catching fluid balance problems early in patients at risk for Tumor Lysis Syndrome?

options.A: Restricting all oral fluids
options.B: Checking blood pressure twice a week
options.C: Weighing the patient once a month
options.D: Tracking daily intake and output

explanation: Strict monitoring of fluid input and output helps nurses evaluate kidney function and hydration status during high-risk treatment periods. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T13#GNS321_U1_T13_h5)

question: What is the main problem in the body that causes diabetes mellitus?

options.A: Defects in insulin production or action
options.B: Overproduction of digestive enzymes
options.C: Excessive secretion of glucagon
options.D: Rapid breakdown of thyroid hormones

explanation: Think of diabetes as a trouble with insulin—either the body isn't making enough of it, or it's not using the insulin it has properly, which leaves too much sugar in the blood. You've got this!

question: Why must everyone step back and not touch the patient while the AED is analyzing or shocking?

options.A: Movement can interfere with rhythm analysis or cause accidental shocks
options.B: Rescuers will catch the electrical current and stop breathing
options.C: The physical vibration of standing nearby stops the machine
options.D: The AED machine requires complete silence to function properly

explanation: Safety rule number one during an AED check: clear everybody! Movement tricks the machine's rhythm reader and can even shock the person touching the patient.

question: In elderly care, why do nurses look at a patient's physical ability rather than just their birth certificate?

options.A: Because chronological age alone does not reflect physical strength or health status
options.B: Because chronological age can be altered easily with basic exercises
options.C: Because hospital funding depends entirely on a patient's exact birth year
options.D: Because physiological age remains identical in every person over sixty

explanation: Spot on! Two people of the exact same age can have very different physical fitness levels depending on their lifelong habits and health.

question: A senior nurse angrily complains during a meeting about new shift scheduling software. What does her anger usually mean?

options.A: She is trying to get her younger colleagues fired from the unit.
options.B: She is feeling vulnerable and cares about her daily workflow.
options.C: She completely lacks basic computer literacy skills.
options.D: She is planning to resign from the hospital by the end of the week.

explanation: Anger during big changes often masks vulnerability. It shows she deeply cares about how her work gets done!

question: What do we call a dangerously low level of oxygen in the blood?

options.A: Hemothorax
options.B: Atelectasis
options.C: Hypoxemia
options.D: Hypercapnia

explanation: Well done! 'Hypo-' means low, and 'oxemia' refers to oxygen in the blood. Put them together and you have hypoxemia.

question: About how many half-lives does it usually take for a drug to be almost completely cleared from the body?

options.A: 4 to 5 half-lives
options.B: 8 to 10 half-lives
options.C: 1 to 2 half-lives
options.D: 12 to 15 half-lives

explanation: You can count on this rule of thumb: after about 4 to 5 half-lives, over 95 percent of the drug is gone, meaning it's practically washed out of the system.

question: What is the main role of a nurse when it comes to ward medical supplies?

options.A: Setting the market prices for incoming hospital drugs
options.B: Manufacturing basic pharmaceuticals for emergency use
options.C: Auditing the financial statements of the hospital board
options.D: Acting as a primary gatekeeper and user of resources

explanation: You handle drugs and supplies right at the bedside every day, which means you play a huge part in monitoring and using them wisely. Great job keeping track of how resources are managed!

question: Which activity is a key community prevention strategy for GBV in displacement settings?

options.A: Establishing safe spaces for women and girls
options.B: Banning all public gatherings and educational meetings
options.C: Locking all community members inside their tents at night
options.D: Stopping all clinical treatment services in displacement camps

explanation: Safe spaces give women and girls a secure area to gather, find peer support, and join community empowerment programs.

question: A community nurse gives out insecticide-treated bed nets to prevent malaria. Which part of the epidemiological triangle is this tackling?

options.A: The genetic makeup
options.B: The infectious agent directly
options.C: The environment
options.D: The host immune system

explanation: Great thinking! Bed nets change the environment where humans and mosquitoes meet, keeping the vector away from you.

question: What is an example of secondary prevention when caring for vulnerable families?

options.A: Punishing parents who miss immunizations
options.B: Screening for early signs of disease like malnutrition or high blood pressure
options.C: Treating severe late-stage illnesses in the ICU
options.D: Building brand new clinics in remote towns

explanation: Correct! Secondary prevention is all about early detection and screening so health issues can be caught and treated early.

question: What is the main job of the air-in-line detector on an infusion pump?

options.A: To measure the exact temperature of the infusing fluid
options.B: To calculate the total fluid volume remaining in the bag
options.C: To stop air bubbles from reaching the patient's bloodstream
options.D: To increase the speed of the fluid if a block occurs

explanation: Spot on! That little sensor is a lifesaver—it catches air bubbles in the tube and stops the pump instantly before air can get into the vein.

question: What is a very important safety step when caring for an elderly patient who just started a tranquilizer?

options.A: Checking blood glucose levels every two hours
options.B: Restricting all fluid intake to prevent nighttime urination
options.C: Encouraging immediate participation in heavy physical exercise
options.D: Implementing strict fall precautions due to sedation and dizziness

explanation: Sedatives make older adults feel dizzy and unsteady on their feet, so keeping them safe from accidental falls is a top nursing priority!

question: How should a nurse best handle a patient who is hesitant about taking a vaccine?

options.A: Use empathetic communication and provide clear, factual information
options.B: Insist that vaccination is mandatory without discussion
options.C: Ignore their concerns and focus only on willing patients
options.D: Warn them that refusal will result in legal penalties

explanation: Listening patiently and addressing fears with kindness and facts is the best way to build trust. Great nursing communication! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T12#GNS214_U1_T12_h8)

question: What word describes an endocrine gland producing way too much hormone?

options.A: Upregulation
options.B: Homeostasis
options.C: Hyposecretion
options.D: Hypersecretion

explanation: Break it down: 'hyper' means high or excessive, and 'secretion' means releasing a substance. So, hypersecretion means too much hormone output!

question: Why do some parasite eggs cause long-term, painful inflammation in body tissues?

options.A: They cause immediate chemical burns on the skin surface.
options.B: They get trapped in organs and trigger immune system reactions.
options.C: They rapidly convert human muscle tissue into adult worms.
options.D: They release large amounts of pure oxygen into the blood cells.

explanation: That's right! Positive pressure gently pushes air outwards whenever the door opens, stopping hallway germs from drifting in.

question: Roughly what percentage of all waste generated in a healthcare facility is non-hazardous general waste?
explanation: You'd be surprised! The vast majority of hospital waste (around 75% to 90%) is actually regular, non-hazardous stuff from everyday operations, just like household trash.

question: A patient asks if fresh eggs and plain milk are okay on a gluten-free diet. What should you tell them?

options.A: Only if they are labeled with a special certification stamp.
options.B: Dairy is allowed, but eggs must be strictly avoided.
options.C: Yes, fresh eggs and plain dairy are naturally free of gluten.
options.D: No, all animal products contain traces of wheat protein.

explanation: Pure, unprocessed whole foods like eggs, meat, and plain milk do not contain gluten naturally. Simple and safe!

question: In maritime healthcare, what does the abbreviation TMAS stand for?

options.A: Transport Medical Action System
options.B: Trauma Management At Sea
options.C: Total Maritime Air Support
options.D: Telemedical Assistance Service

explanation: You got it! TMAS connects ships at sea with land-based medical experts for remote guidance and advice.

question: Which agency coordinates primary healthcare development at the national level in Nigeria?

options.A: National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA)
options.B: Federal Ministry of Works and Housing
options.C: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control
options.D: Nigerian Medical Association (NMA)

explanation: The NPHCDA is the main federal body guiding PHC implementation all across Nigeria. Good to know for Nigerian nursing practice!

question: How does dropping out of school early increase a young person's risk of delinquency?

options.A: It leaves them idle and vulnerable to negative peer influences
options.B: It guarantees immediate employment in illegal syndicates
options.C: It directly damages the physical structures of the brain
options.D: It removes all legal protections granted to citizens

explanation: Makes total sense! When kids are out of school with too much free time and no positive guidance, they easily fall in with the wrong crowd.

question: Why must nurses pre-test health posters and flyers with the local community before printing thousands of copies?

options.A: To calculate the exact salary of the project nurses and staff
options.B: To guarantee that the printed posters are waterproof and durable
options.C: To ensure the messages are culturally appropriate and easily understood
options.D: To comply with international tax laws for healthcare projects

explanation: Spot on! Pre-testing saves you from printing confusing or offensive messages by catching misunderstandings early.

question: A nurse finishes emptying a utility bin filled with used dressings and removes her heavy utility gloves. What is the immediate next step she should take?

options.A: Drink clean water to prevent dehydration
options.B: Perform hand hygiene with soap and water or alcohol rub
options.C: Write an incident report in the ward register
options.D: Put on a fresh pair of sterile surgical gloves

explanation: Hand hygiene is always mandatory immediately after taking off gloves, as microscopic tears in gloves can let germs reach the skin. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h8)

question: Instead of using long, direct quotes from research articles, what is generally preferred?

options.A: Omitting the authors' names completely to save writing space
options.B: Rewriting the data with different numbers to make it sound better
options.C: Paraphrasing the authors' ideas in your own professional words
options.D: Translating the quotes into a different language for variety

explanation: Paraphrasing shows you truly understand the concepts and helps your paper flow smoothly. You're doing great!

question: Why must you always keep a patient's culture and pocket (financial status) in mind when giving dietary advice?

options.A: Hospital accreditation agencies legally mandate recording patient income
options.B: Low-income patients are exempt from following strict therapeutic diets
options.C: Dietary plans that ignore these factors are much less likely to be followed
options.D: Cultural foods always contain hidden chemicals that alter blood test results

explanation: If you recommend foreign foods or things they cannot afford to buy in the market, they simply won't do it. Tailor your advice to what is accessible and familiar to them!

question: Why do differing goals cause friction in collaborative health projects?

options.A: One partner prioritizes financial return while another prioritizes equity
options.B: It automatically increases patient wait times in private clinics
options.C: It prevents hospitals from purchasing any medications
options.D: It forces all nurses to switch from public to private employment

explanation: When one partner cares mostly about profit and another cares mostly about equal access for everyone, it can be tricky to agree on budgets and pricing.

question: Why must data collection instruments be valid and reliable in cross-sectional research?

options.A: To make sure patients take their medications on time
options.B: To guarantee that the study takes at least five years to finish
options.C: To prevent the researcher from having to use statistics
options.D: To ensure the measurements are accurate and consistent

explanation: Validity and reliability simply mean your measuring tool actually tests what it's supposed to, and gives steady results every time.

question: What is the primary purpose of drug legislation in nursing?

options.A: To increase the cost of essential medicines
options.B: Um, to reduce the workload of hospital pharmacists
options.C: To make medication administration slower
options.D: To protect the public and healthcare workers

explanation: Drug laws exist mainly to keep patients safe from harm and guide nurses on legal medication practices. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T13#GNS122_U1_T13_h1)

question: What is the best way to handle giving a positive HIV result to a patient?

options.A: Deliver the news calmly and allow time for emotional processing
options.B: Insist that they call their family members into the room at once
options.C: Immediately list every available medication side effect in detail
options.D: Quickly hand over the paper lab report and ask them to leave

explanation: Spot on! Hearing this news is heavy. Patients need a calm, supportive space and time to process their emotions.

question: Which of these is NOT a typical emotional stage when adjusting to a life-changing disability?

options.A: Anger
options.B: Instant euphoria
options.C: Denial
options.D: Depression

explanation: You're doing great! People don't just jump straight to joy; they usually move through shock, denial, anger, and sadness first.

question: Why is quitting smoking considered 'primary prevention' rather than 'secondary prevention'?

options.A: It is only performed after a patient receives a confirmed cancer diagnosis.
options.B: It relies entirely on surgical removal of damaged bronchial tissue.
options.C: It focuses on finding small tumors before symptoms appear.
options.D: It aims to prevent the disease from ever developing in the first place.

explanation: Brilliant! Primary prevention stops harmful exposures (like tobacco) so the disease process never even gets a chance to start.

question: What are the three core elements that make a study a true experimental design?

options.A: Manipulation, control, and randomization
options.B: Sampling, blinding, and qualitative coding
options.C: Observation, interview, and transcription
options.D: Surveying, coding, and theme generation

explanation: A true experiment needs these three: you manipulate a variable, control outside factors, and randomly assign your participants. Great revision practice!

question: A patient gets a known surgical complication even though you followed all safety rules. Is this malpractice?

options.A: No, but the hospital must still pay financial compensation
options.B: No, because the nurse followed the accepted standard of care
options.C: Yes, because any bad outcome in the hospital is malpractice
options.D: Yes, because the patient suffered physical harm during care

explanation: A bad outcome doesn't automatically mean malpractice. If you did your job correctly and followed standard protocols, you're in the clear!

question: A nurse is caring for a patient admitted with a highly contagious airborne respiratory infection. Which precaution is NOT appropriate for this specific case?

options.A: Housing the patient inside a negative pressure isolation room
options.B: Placing the patient in a standard open ward bed with no barriers
options.C: Ensuring healthcare workers wear fitted N95 respirator masks
options.D: Limiting visitor access to protect other vulnerable patients

explanation: Airborne infections require negative pressure rooms and specialized masks, not open wards where droplet nuclei can easily infect others. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h7)

question: Why must nurses look beyond vital signs when assessing a patient?

options.A: Doctors handle physical assessments while nurses only do paperwork
options.B: Physical numbers do not show how the patient emotionally experiences the disease
options.C: Vital signs are completely useless in clinical nursing practice
options.D: Patients never tell the truth about their physical pain levels

explanation: Vital signs tell us about the body, but talking to the patient tells us about their fears, coping skills, and emotional state.

question: How do Standard Precautions differ from original Universal Precautions?

options.A: Standard Precautions remove the need for handwashing if gloves are worn
options.B: Standard Precautions apply to all body fluids and moist tissues, not just blood
options.C: Standard Precautions ignore non-intact skin and focus solely on respiratory droplets
options.D: Standard Precautions are only used when a patient has a confirmed laboratory diagnosis

explanation: While Universal Precautions focused mainly on blood, Standard Precautions broaden the safety net to include all body fluids, secretions, and non-intact skin for every patient. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h1)

question: What type of receptors do smell molecules (odorants) bind to on the tiny hairs in our nose?

options.A: Voltage-gated calcium channels
options.B: Ligand-gated mechanical pores
options.C: G-protein coupled receptors
options.D: Steroid hormone receptors

explanation: You're doing great! Odorants lock into special G-protein coupled receptors on the olfactory cilia, triggering a chemical cascade that lets our brain know we're smelling something.

question: What is a major clinical benefit when a husband knows basic pregnancy danger signs?

options.A: He can arrange timely transport during an emergency.
options.B: He can diagnose malaria without laboratory tests.
options.C: He can safely perform a delivery at home if needed.
options.D: He can prescribe iron supplements to his wife.

explanation: Spotting danger signs early means partners can act fast and avoid deadly delays in reaching the hospital. Brilliant!

question: Which of the following is a classic example of an obstetric emergency?

options.A: Severe postpartum hemorrhage
options.B: Chronic knee osteoarthritis
options.C: A mild seasonal allergy
options.D: Routine pregnancy checkup

explanation: Heavy bleeding after childbirth is a life-threatening emergency unique to obstetric care. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T1#GNS315_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why is a pregnant teenager at a much higher risk for nutritional shortages than an adult pregnant woman?

options.A: She is still growing herself and must compete with the fetus for nutrients.
options.B: Adult women require half the daily calories of teenagers.
options.C: Her digestive tract is shorter and absorbs fewer vitamins overall.
options.D: Hormones during teen pregnancy completely block fat digestion.

explanation: Correct! The teen's body is still finishing its own growth spurt while also feeding a growing baby, creating a huge demand for extra nutrients.

question: Why is taking a good patient history considered the bedrock of your clinical nursing practice?

options.A: It provides definitive proof of a medical diagnosis
options.B: It replaces the need for any laboratory investigations
options.C: It guides your physical assessment and care planning
options.D: It eliminates all risks of clinical documentation errors

explanation: Spot on! A thorough history points you in the right direction, helping you know where to focus your physical exam and how to plan the best care.

question: What is the medical term for when puberty starts much earlier than usual?

options.A: Delayed puberty
options.B: Hypothyroidism
options.C: Precocious puberty
options.D: Acromegaly

explanation: Spot on! 'Precocious' simply means happening earlier than expected, referring here to an unusually early start to puberty.

question: What does interpersonal conflict mean?

options.A: Fighting between hospital management and unions
options.B: Arguments within a person's own thoughts
options.C: Disagreements between two or more individuals
options.D: Rivalry between two different departments

explanation: Interpersonal conflict simply means friction or clashing between separate people. Simple and clear!

question: Which of these is NOT a risk factor for getting Korsakoff syndrome?

options.A: Regular aerobic exercise
options.B: Hyperemesis gravidarum
options.C: Chronic alcohol abuse
options.D: Prolonged malnutrition

explanation: Exercise keeps you healthy! It doesn't cause vitamin shortages, unlike severe vomiting, poor diet, or heavy drinking.

question: What are the two primary functions of the ovaries?

options.A: Digest nutrients and absorb water
options.B: Filter waste and produce urine
options.C: Pump blood through the pelvic floor
options.D: Produce eggs and secrete sex hormones

explanation: Ovaries serve as both glands that make hormones (estrogen and progesterone) and storage sites for female eggs. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h6)

question: How does Hodgkin lymphoma typically spread compared to non-Hodgkin types?

options.A: It only affects organs in the lower belly
options.B: It never spreads outside the bone marrow
options.C: It spreads in an orderly, predictable pattern
options.D: It jumps randomly to distant body parts immediately

explanation: Hodgkin lymphoma is like a polite traveler—it usually moves step-by-step to neighboring lymph nodes, making its path pretty predictable.

question: What is the primary purpose of monitoring a Behavioural Change Communication program?

options.A: To ensure resources are well-spent and goals are met
options.B: To punish staff members who arrive late to work
options.C: To increase the cost of community health services
options.D: To eliminate the need for future community meetings

explanation: Correct! Monitoring helps nurses track progress, see if the program is working, and make smart adjustments along the way.

question: A patient calls three days after her polypectomy reporting mild lower belly cramps and very light pink spotting. What should the nurse say?

options.A: Schedule an emergency surgical re-exploration
options.B: Advise her to start taking oral antibiotics right away
options.C: Instruct her to report immediately to the emergency room
options.D: Reassure her that this is a normal, expected finding

explanation: A little bit of cramping and light spotting is totally normal after the cervix has been touched or treated. Just reassure and comfort her!

question: If Florence Nightingale could whisper advice to you on the ward today, what would she say is the true focus of nursing?

options.A: Diagnosing rare tropical medical diseases
options.B: Manipulating the patient's environment to promote healing
options.C: Performing major surgical procedures
options.D: Administering complex intravenous medications

explanation: You got it! Nightingale was all about fresh air, clean water, and bright light. She believed in setting up the environment so the patient's body could heal itself.

question: A patient on a strong psychiatric medication suddenly gets severe muscle stiffness and spasms. What drug class will the doctor most likely order?

options.A: Short-acting insulins
options.B: Broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.C: Intravenous anticoagulants
options.D: Central anticholinergics

explanation: Brilliant! Anticholinergics are the go-to treatment for those pesky extrapyramidal side effects (muscle spasms and stiffness) caused by some antipsychotic drugs.

question: What is a major financial headache caused by unreliable public electricity in Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Automatic shutdown of all nursing schools
options.B: Heavy financial expenditure on diesel generators
options.C: Immediate reduction in patient admission rates
options.D: Instant conversion of hospitals to digital clinics

explanation: Spot on! Hospitals have to spend a massive chunk of their budgets buying diesel just to keep emergency lights and life-saving machines running.

question: What is the core philosophy of Primary Health Care (PHC)?

options.A: Bringing essential health services as close as possible to where people live
options.B: Focusing treatment exclusively on patients who can pay cash
options.C: Relying entirely on foreign medical aid for community survival
options.D: Building high-tech specialist hospitals in major metropolitan cities

explanation: PHC emphasizes grassroots accessibility, making basic health promotion and disease prevention available to everyone in the community. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h6)

question: A nurse plans to visit a client living in a remote area with a history of unpredictable aggression. What is the safest action?

options.A: Ignore the history of aggression because home environments are safe
options.B: Go together with a colleague and inform the clinic supervisor
options.C: Send a text message asking the client to come to the clinic instead
options.D: Visit alone very early in the morning before the client wakes up

explanation: Traveling with a partner and notifying supervisors are key safety protocols when visiting clients with a history of aggression. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T6#GNS314_U4_T6_h2)

question: What does the term ACE stand for when studying childhood and mental health?

options.A: Acute Clinical Evaluation
options.B: Adverse Childhood Experiences
options.C: Affective Coping Environment
options.D: Anxiety and Crisis Education

explanation: ACE stands for Adverse Childhood Experiences—tough or traumatic events that happen before a person turns eighteen.

question: A patient comes to the clinic with ongoing pelvic pain and high anxiety, and hints point toward past abuse. What does this show us?

options.A: That physical injuries from violence always heal completely in a few weeks
options.B: That mental health struggles never cause physical pain in the body
options.C: That chronic physical symptoms and emotional trauma are often connected
options.D: That the patient is just making up symptoms to get drugs

explanation: Spot on! Violence often leaves lasting physical pain right alongside deep emotional scars, which is why holistic nursing care is so important.

question: How often should you check and record temperatures in a clinic's vaccine refrigerator?

options.A: Twice daily
options.B: Every hour
options.C: Only on weekends
options.D: Once a week

explanation: Checking temperatures twice a day helps us catch fridge issues early and keeps our vaccine supply safe for the community!
